facts.fact: Malawi24 reports that UNDP handed the government 152 printers in Lilongwe on 9 October 2026 to decentralise birth, marriage and death registration, 100 for National Registration Bureau offices at Traditional Authority level and 52 for health facilities.
facts.system: NRB birth, marriage and death registration services

facts.fact: The homeland security minister said 180 health facilities have already been digitalised, with work under way to extend registration services through traditional and sub-traditional authorities; the document gives no total and does not say what digitalised means or that the facilities register births there (no date given; published date used).
facts.system: NRB birth, marriage and death registration services

facts.fact: The printers were supplied by UNDP through the Inclusive Digital Transformation for Malawi project, financed by the European Union, Norway and Ireland.
facts.system: NRB birth, marriage and death registration services
